name: Shethar
overview: Shethar is a male figure identified as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media, as noted in the book of Esther. There is no additional tribal affiliation or personal notes recorded about him, limiting our understanding to his political and regional significance in the biblical text.
namesAndTitles: The name Shethar appears as a proper name in Esther 1:14. There is no specific meaning or divine origin indicated for this name in the scriptural record, so it is simply recognized as a proper name without further elaboration.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Shethar beyond his designation as one of the seven princes of Persia and Media. No other personal or familial connections are documented in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Shethar's significance lies in his role as one of the seven princes who served under King Ahasuerus, representing the governance and administrative structure of Persia and Media during the events of Esther. His mention underscores the political hierarchy and the broader context in which the narrative unfolds, highlighting the earthly authorities present during God's providential work.
